**Resubmitted: deviation (T4C), fallback target, two operations — validated `ok:true`, minimality clean.**

The single repair in this pass targets the deterministic failure ("Customer convenience termination present"), by adopting the verifier's clarity wording so the Company's right is express rather than inferred:

**Op 1 — §4.1 (p0024).** Rendered: "...unless terminated **upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other, by the Company for convenience at any time or by HDI only at the end of a term.**"
- Restores "to the other" (previously dropped).
- Uses the words "for convenience" and attributes them to the Company, at any time — so the right cannot be argued down to a non-renewal mechanic buried in the auto-renewal sentence.
- Keeps the same 90 days for both parties and confines HDI to the end of a term.

**Op 2 — §4.2(a) (p0026).** Unchanged from the accepted version: the three-month Section 3.1 fee ceiling as prong (ii) of a "lesser of", with the original Net Sales computation preserved as prong (i), so §4.2(b)'s zero-or-less netting still yields no payment at or below $800,000 of trailing Net Sales. §4.2(c), the Termination Date definition and the renewal structure remain untouched.

Coverage is at fallback with all four elements carried by operative language (elements 1, 3, 4 by Op 1; element 2 by Op 2). Preferred remains unclaimed — notice stays at 90 rather than 30 days and no refund sentence was added, there being no prepaid fees under the revenue-share model. The §4.2(a)-versus-breach point stays in the comment as a note, not drafted in, since it sits outside the checklist.
